newsitem.title: SUDAN: Pro-Sudan forces say defeated rebels in a battle.
newsitem.headline: Pro-Sudan forces say defeated rebels in a battle.

text.p: A Sudanese newspaper said on Saturday forces loyal to the Khartoum government inflicted a "crushing defeat" on the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) of John Garang.

The private newspaper Alwan said that SPLA/Bahr al-Ghazal group of Kerubino Kwanyin Bol inflicted on Garang's forces "a crushing defeat in a battle which took place this month in the area of Wunrog, northeast of Gogrial".
Wunrog is about 100 km (60 miles) north of Wau, the south's second largest town.

The Arabic daily quoted Faustino Atem, a commander of the Bahr al-Ghazal group, as saying Garang's forces fled when 11 of their officers were killed. He added his forces seized a large number of arms and military equipment.
The report could not be independently confirmed.
The Bahr al-Ghazal group, which has split from the SPLA, and at least three other rebel groups are due to sign a peace agreement with the Sudan government in the next few days.
The mainstream SPLA refuses to sign an agreement with the government, which it has been fighting for almost 13 years.
